display.title: Tanya Shiur 56: Chapter 23, Mitzvos as the King's Limbs, and Ahavas Yisroel
display.summary_short: A Yiddish shiur on Tanya chapter 23, on mitzvos as Hashem's innermost will, followed by a talk on the Rebbe's Kuntres Ahavas Yisroel and loving every Jew.
display.summary_long: Shiur 56 in Rabbi Yosef Goldstein's Yiddish Tanya series. It opens with Torah as light and Chassidus as its inner light, teaching the difference between the inner and the outer side of things, like the soul and the body. Tanya chapter 23 distinguishes Hashem's inner will from His outer will, illustrated by a man who works only for the satisfaction his wages bring: Hashem's deepest desire is a dwelling in this world, fulfilled through the 613 mitzvos. The Zohar calls the Torah one with Hashem, and the Tikkunim call the mitzvos the 'limbs of the King'; all the worlds draw their life from a Jew's mitzvah, as the Frierdiker Rebbe explained the words 'Baruch Atah Hashem'. Just as a hand moves instantly at a person's will, a mitzvah is wholly nullified to Hashem's will. The second part, given at a listener's request, is a talk on the Kuntres Ahavas Yisroel that the Rebbe asked to be printed and spread: the Baal Shem Tov's teaching to love every single Jew, the Alter Rebbe's mashal of a rusted gold cup, the Rambam's laws of loving a fellow Jew and a convert, the Arizal's instruction to accept this mitzvah before davening, and the Rebbe Rashab's answer to his son's bar mitzvah question.
display.lesson: Every mitzvah joins a Jew to Hashem's innermost will, and loving every Jew, seeing the gold beneath the rust, opens the gates for our prayers.

study_text.note: Daf 28; the class stops at the third line. The second half is a talk on Ahavas Yisroel.

segments.title: Torah as light: the inner and the outer
segments.summary: Chassidus shows the inner side of everything, as the soul is the true person and the body its covering.

segments.title: Hashem's inner will and outer will
segments.summary: A worker wants the satisfaction, not the work itself; so too Hashem's inner desire is a dwelling below through the 613 mitzvos.

segments.title: Torah is one with Hashem; mitzvos are the King's limbs
segments.summary: The Zohar and the Tikkunim, and how all the worlds wait for a Jew's mitzvah, as in the Frierdiker Rebbe's teaching on 'Baruch Atah'.

segments.title: The mashal of the hand and the soul
segments.summary: A limb moves instantly at a person's will, just as a mitzvah is wholly nullified to Hashem's will.

segments.title: The Rebbe's Kuntres Ahavas Yisroel
segments.summary: The Rebbe asked that the booklet on Ahavas Yisroel be printed and spread to as many Jews as possible.

segments.title: Loving every Jew: the Baal Shem Tov and the rusted gold cup
segments.summary: The Baal Shem Tov's emphasis on every single Jew and the Alter Rebbe's mashal of gold hidden under rust.

segments.title: The Rambam on loving a fellow Jew and a convert
segments.summary: Speak of others' praise, guard their money and honor, and love the convert as Hashem loves him.

segments.title: Accepting Ahavas Yisroel before davening
segments.summary: The Arizal's instruction and why united prayers rise together like Yaakov's ladder.

segments.title: The Rebbe Rashab's answer at a bar mitzvah
segments.summary: Love between Jews is the King's greatest nachas, the key that opens the gates for prayer.
